How much affect does the terrain have on the gameplay? Right now we have Megalopolis and Insula Primalis. From what I've read thus far my impression is that in a skirmish they would functionally just provide a varying arrangement of hights accross which the battle rages. Right now its a city and a wild jungle as options.

Some environment decks don't seem like they'd scale well to Tactics terrain hex scale.

I don't see Blade's Mobile Defense Platform or the Freedom 5 tower translating well (given the Freedom 5 tower is currently represented as about 4 hexes big). It would be cool of the Mobile Defense Platform were a separate hex piece that had rules for moving over the other terrain...a moveable section of level 5 height or something that can be moved by the villain across the battle field.

Storywise I don't see the Wild West or Final Wasteland envrionments available given the story hints so far show a contained single timeline.

I love the effect environment decks have on the Card Game and I hope that is still felt with Tactics.

Well I haven't seen an actual game in action. Perhaps you have had a chance to play test and liked what you saw. I am not saying that the game won't work just fine the size it is. However, I have played quite a few miniature games and there are several advantages to a bigger board. It is not just bigger for bigger's sake as you suggest.

1) A larger area gives you more room for tactical maneuvering allowing for greater strategies to emerge. Especially when new/different combinations of characters are employed.

2) You can adapt and play larger games or have more variety in the terrain when you maintain the smaller size. Playing on the same board is totally fine, but who doesn’t want more variety.

3) With bigger you normally get a grander thematic feeling. If bigger was just bigger than why not just have Omnitron occupy 1 hex? Is he just bigger for bigger's sake? No! He is soooo much cooler being the big robot that we imagine him/it as.

Yes, games will go faster if you have an artificially compressed battlefield. Area of effect powers will catch more bad guys (or god guys), the enemy is always within range, etc. I know that I can use one of my play mats to create my own environments to play on (and I probably will), but they will never be as cool as ones created by GTG. Even now I can see Spiff creating maps to be printed on card stock and cut into game pieces, so maybe that will be the answer to my desire.

At the end of the day what really would be wrong with more terrain?

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
I find it less inflammatory to state one's opinions and feelings than to make claims about another person and or his/her statements.

 

For instance, I think I would find it more palatable if someone told me that my remarks made them feel as if their opinions were being dismissed than if I were told that I was being snobbish.

 

I am very excited for Sentinel Tactics. One concern I have, however, is that every game will quickly devolve into all of the characters running  up and just trying to hit each other as hard as they can. Though a playtester, I've only played a handful of games and all of those were skirmishes rather than scenarios, so I hold a lot of hope that with more experience I'll start to see more (as well as more nuanced) tactics and strategies in my games.

 

I wonder if the OPs point about a larger game board might, indeed help. While I agree with other respondents' that at least some if not most of the time having a larger board will simply mean a delay in the action getting started, I can see room for other situations -- things like leading part of the opposition a significant distance away from a crucial point on the map or splitting one's characters such that an opponent is forced to comit to two smaller skirmishes rather than one larger one.
